title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying automorphisms u of the profinite group \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}. This group is generated by σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3) and is the extension of S_3 by \hat\pi_{0,3} = \hat\pi_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}). He imposes u(σ_∞)=σ_∞ and u(ρ)=gρ. This is the 'équation des lacets' set-up: Grothendieck–Teichmüller type data (λ, ξ, γ, β). In it, 2γ+1 = p plays the role of the cyclotomic exponent and must lie in \hat Z^×. The previous page reduces everything to a single delicate equation (C) in γ∈\hat Z, given λ. There are two cases, according to which formula (B) defines ξ from λ: ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} or ξ = λ l_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1}.

On this page he predicts how the two cases split. They should correspond to p ≡ 1 or p ≡ −1 mod 3; p ≡ 0 is excluded since p is a unit. Since p = 2γ+1, this is 2γ ≡ 0 or −2, i.e. γ ≡ 0 or −1 mod 3. He also notes that γ ≡ 1 mod 3 is forbidden, since it would force 3 | p. He expects this to hold at least when u ∈ Γ_{l_0} (automorphisms respecting the inertia class of l_0).

To test it he passes to a finite (or more tractable) quotient. Here l_0 = (σ_∞ρ)^2, so imposing l_0^3 = 1 means (σ_∞ρ)^6 = 1. The S_3-symmetry then also gives l_1^3 = l_∞^3 = 1. The kernel becomes the (3,3,3) triangle group ⟨l_0,l_1,l_∞ | l_i^3 = 1, l_∞l_1l_0 = 1⟩. This is the Euclidean (wallpaper) group, the orbifold fundamental group attached to the Fermat cubic / j=0 elliptic curve.

As a better alternative, he uses \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^∧ (the modular-group description, with π_{0,3} as a level-2 congruence subgroup). He then reduces to level 6, SL(2,Z/6) ≅ SL(2,Z/2) × SL(2,Z/3) by CRT, primed for a suitable quotient. In this finite group the mod-3 behaviour of γ (i.e. p mod 3, the mod-3 cyclotomic character) can be read off by explicit matrix computation. The next page notes this requires identifying σ_∞ and ρ as explicit matrices in SL(2,\hat Z).
errors: No mathematical error in the congruence bookkeeping: p=2γ+1 ≡ 1 ⇔ γ ≡ 0, p ≡ −1 ⇔ γ ≡ −1, and γ ≡ 1 ⇒ 3|p are all correct.

The prime in 'Sl(2,Z/6Z)' ≃ Sl(2,Z/2Z) × Sl(2,Z/3Z)'' is ambiguous. If it means the commutator subgroup, the SL(2,Z/2) factor should also be primed (giving Z/3 × Q_8). More likely it denotes a quotient such as mod ±1. The notation is unclear but not an error per se.
The claim that the two (B)-cases correspond exactly to p mod 3 is stated as a prediction ('Je prévois'), not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Splitting the two solution types of the 'equation of loops' (ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} vs λ l_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1}) according to the cyclotomic exponent p = 2γ+1 mod 3.
ideas.modern_name: Mod-3 cyclotomic character constraint in GT-type relations (the hexagon/ρ-relation with ρ of order 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for \hat{GT}; mod-n reductions studied by Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps and others

ideas.what: Testing by reduction to the (3,3,3) triangle group extended by S_3, i.e. imposing l_i^3 = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the orbifold fundamental group of the Fermat cubic / j=0 elliptic curve quotient

ideas.what: Using \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^∧ and reducing to level 6 via SL(2,Z/6) ≅ SL(2,Z/2) × SL(2,Z/3).
ideas.modern_name: Modular-group / congruence-quotient description of the S_3-extended profinite π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Γ(2) free of rank 2); used in GT literature (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Longue Marche / Esquisse (SL(2,Z) and the modular tower)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page: routine congruence bookkeeping plus a plan to test a prediction via a finite congruence quotient. The ideas (GT-type relations, (3,3,3) triangle group, SL(2,Z) level-6 reduction) are standard in later Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature. No finished new result appears.
transcription_corrections: 'C'est un tour cas ce qui sera le cas si u ∈ Γ_{l_0}' should read 'C'est en tout cas ce qui sera le cas si u ∈ Γ_{l_0}'.
The crossed-out object after 'réduisons le' precedes \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3}; the struck line 'l_0^3 = l_1^3 = l_∞^3 = 1 ...' is correctly marked as deleted.
'(l_∞ l_1 l_0) = 1' is as written; it is the product relation.
